acceptance: Red test first: a fenced write leaves <workspace>/fence-reverted.patch, and `git apply` of it on the dispatched tree gives back the reverted content.
The fence diagnostic names the patch path.
A run with no fenced write writes no patch file.

consumed.resolution: lane triage recorded it as shipped (lane triage (cycle 2184) skip_shipped: git_sha 366059d65)

fix: Before the restore, write `git diff --binary` of the reverted paths (and the content of each untracked reverted file) to <workspace>/fence-reverted.patch, and name that path in the diagnostic. Keep the restore itself unchanged.
source: console, 2026-11-03: agent run console-builder (agent-console-builder-20261102T232631Z-98ea) wrote 10 files of a full H9 build in 12 min; the fence restored all 10 and kept no diff in the workspace
summary: treefence (go/internal/treefence/fence.go:376) restores each out-of-scope write to the dispatched tree and logs the path list only. The run workspace keeps no patch, so the work of the seat is lost and the run must start again. On 2026-11-03 this cost one console-builder run of about 12 min and 5.2 M cache-read tokens.
title: The worktree fence saves the patch of each write it reverts, so a fenced build is never lost
